name: Kalkals
subtitle: little curls of coconut-milk dough deep-fried crisp and frosted with sugar, the Christmas sweet

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp for the dough, plus 250g for the glaze

prepNotes: Kalkals are rolled on the back of a fork, and it takes a few to get the knack. Make one, see how it curls, then adjust how hard you press.
The dough must rest at least 2 hours, or overnight refrigerated. Unrested dough is slack and the curls unravel in the oil.
Have everything ready before you start the sugar syrup at the end; it goes from clear to grainy in under a minute.

steps.text: Rub the melted ghee into the maida, rava, 3 tbsp sugar, cardamom and salt with your fingertips until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs.
Work in the beaten egg, then add the coconut milk a little at a time until you have a firm, smooth dough. You may not need all of it.
steps.tip: Firm, like a stiff chapati dough. A soft dough will not hold the ridges.

steps.text: Knead 5 minutes, cover and rest at least 2 hours.
Pinch off marble-sized pieces. Roll each into a tiny ball, press it flat on the back of a greased fork, then roll it away from you with your thumb so it curls into a shell.
steps.tip: Press lightly. Bear down and the dough sticks to the fork instead of curling.

steps.text: Spread the shaped kalkals on a tray in a single layer and leave them to dry, uncovered, for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a kadhai to a steady medium — a scrap of dough should rise slowly and sizzle, not brown in seconds.
steps.tip: If they brown fast they will be raw inside. Low and slow gives an even, pale gold crisp.

steps.text: Fry in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until pale gold and hard. Drain on paper and cool completely.
Boil the 250g sugar with the water to a thick syrup: it is ready when a drop cooled on a plate forms a soft ball between your fingers.
Take the syrup off the heat, tip in the cooled kalkals and stir constantly as the syrup crystallises into a white frosting, 2 to 3 minutes.
steps.tip: Keep stirring right through the grainy stage or they will set in one solid lump.

steps.text: Spread them out on a tray to dry and harden for an hour before storing.

storage: Keep 3 weeks in an airtight tin at room temperature, which is how they survive the whole of Christmas. Do not refrigerate: the sugar frosting goes damp and sticky.
